concepts.def: Migration into a country, often discussed in relation to asile (asylum) and integration.
The process of becoming part of the host society; linked to citoyenneté (citizenship).
Undocumented immigrant ('without papers'); politically charged term in France.
Mood used after il faut que, je veux que, bien que, pour que, sans que, à condition que.
Would have done: aurais/aurait/auraient + past participle. Used in counterfactuals.
Process by which undocumented migrants obtain legal status — debated under successive French governments.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Theme 3: Immigration and the Multicultural French Society — a core area of A-Level French.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Theme 3: Immigration and the Multicultural French Society brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Theme 3: Immigration and the Multicultural French Society.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which French verb form correctly says 'I would have helped' (j'... aidé)?
options: aurai
aurais
avait
étais

mcqs.q: Which conjunction always triggers the subjunctive?
options: parce que
car
bien que
puisque

mcqs.q: What is the difference between 'le' and 'lui' as pronouns?
options: Dans France.
Le replaces a direct object (him/it); lui replaces an indirect object (to him/her).
They are interchangeable.
Le is masculine, lui is feminine.
Dans France.
À France.
Le is masculine, lui is feminine.
En France.

mcqs.q: How do you say 'I play the piano' vs 'I play football'?
options: Le is masculine, lui is feminine.
Je joue DU piano (instrument) vs je joue AU football (sport).
Je joue le piano, je joue le football.
Same preposition for both - 'je joue piano', 'je joue football'.
